title: The Kawhi Anomaly
x_thread: Kawhi Leonard, at 34 years old, went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute. His impact score, how much he helps per minute versus an average NBA minute, went from +0.86 to +2.17. No player 34 or older has ever gained that much in one season.

Historically, only eight players have surged to star level after 31, and none of them kept three-quarters of that gain the next season; Steve Nash kept the most, 45%. Kawhi's surge came in two parts, a heavier role and hotter shooting, and those two parts age differently.

Before tip-off, we put four calls on his season, and each one gets graded in public:
65% his true shooting falls below .610 (he shot .629 last season)
60% his usage stays at 30% or more
50% he stays top 8 in The 644, July 2027 edition
30% he finishes top 8 in Box Plus/Minus

The bigger role usually lasts. The hot shooting, a career-high 52% from mid-range per Cleaning the Glass, usually fades. We published this on October 6, before tip-off. The full piece is free:
https://thegravityreport.com/notes/kawhi/

Kawhi Leonard, at 34 years old, went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute. His impact score, which measures how much a player helps per minute compared with an average NBA minute, went from +0.86 to +2.17. No player 34 or older has ever gained that much in one season, and he is the only star since 1978 to set career highs in usage and true shooting in the same season after 33.

Historically, only eight players have surged to star level after 31, and none of them kept three-quarters of that gain the next season; Steve Nash kept the most, 45%. # r/torontoraptors (post by hand; read the sub's self-promotion rules first)

**Title:** Before the season, we put numbers on Kawhi Leonard. Here's what we're watching

**Body:**

The season is underway. On October 6, before tip-off, we put four calls on Kawhi Leonard's year. Each one gets graded in public.

Kawhi Leonard went from a good starter to the fifth-best player in the league per minute, at 34. No player 34 or older has ever jumped that far in one season.

Late surges have an unkind history. Eight players surged to star level after 31. None kept three-quarters of the improvement the next season.

His surge came in two parts: a heavier role and hotter shooting. His bigger role usually lasts. His hot shooting usually doesn't.

What we said:
65%  His true shooting falls below .610
60%  His usage stays at 30% or more
50%  He stays top 8 in The 644
30%  He finishes top 8 in Box Plus/Minus

Full piece, from October 6 (free, no ads): https://thegravityreport.com/notes/kawhi/

Happy to answer questions about the method in the comments.
